scenes.title: Keep anchors and accent the additions

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps on the test device with Merge Shape set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, on steps 1 to 4) is saved as the protected Anchor: its steps always play as written. Pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Add amount is how many additions are admitted and Add accent scales their velocity. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

steps.title: Read Add amount and Add accent
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Add amount, which reads 100: every candidate addition is admitted. Turn E2 two detents on to Add accent, which reads 70 and scales the velocity of the added trigs to 70 percent. Both settings are already at these values; you only read them here. The grid shows the anchors on steps 1 to 4 and the additions on steps 5 and 7.

steps.title: Hear anchors and additions
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two eight-step loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays the four anchors, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, then two additions as MIDI 60 at velocity 70, shown in the strip below. Anchor velocities are untouched; only the added notes use Add accent.

steps.title: Lower Add accent to 40
steps.caption: Turn E3 left 30 detents. Add accent reads 40; press K3 to apply it, as the sequencer is stopped.

steps.title: Hear quieter additions
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. The four anchors are exactly as before, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, but the two additions are now MIDI 60 at velocity 40 in the strip below, quieter than the 70 you heard before.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps on the test device with Merge Shape set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, on steps 1 to 4) is the protected Anchor and pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) offers additions; both are assigned. Add amount is 100 and Add accent 70, so all candidate additions are allowed and sound at 70 percent of their velocity. The Phrase settings are still at their defaults, the norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

steps.title: Set Cycles to 2
steps.caption: Press E1 once to the Phrase screen, turn E2 to Phrase and press K3. A cycle is one pass of the eight-step loop. Turn E3 once to set Cycles to 2.

steps.title: Choose the Build shape
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Shape and E3 once to choose BUILD, which reads Cycle 1 50 and Cycle 2 100.

steps.title: Apply the phrase
steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED.

steps.title: Loop 1 adds one note
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen. The first loop plays steps 1 to 4 plus one addition (step 7), five notes in the strip below.

steps.title: Loop 2 adds both
steps.caption: The second loop plays steps 1 to 4 plus both additions (steps 5 and 7), six notes. Keep listening to at least four loops, then tap Stop.

steps.title: Build over two channel loops
steps.caption: The two loops keep alternating: the strip below shows the notes of each pass, loop 1 with step 7 added and loop 2 with steps 5 and 7 added, back to the first anchor at the end.

scenes.title: Let each fragment keep its source notes

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays through the test device on an 8-step loop at 90 BPM, rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6. Both patterns are assigned to channel 1 and Strategy is still SKIP. Merge modes is open for channel 1. In this scene a Seed makes a repeatable draw of which pattern each fragment comes from: the same seed always gives the same choice.

steps.title: Choose Fragments
steps.caption: Select Strategy and turn E3 to FRAGMENTS. Strategy and Active both read FRAGMENTS: the loop will be cut into fragments and each fragment will come from one source pattern, chosen by the Seed.

steps.title: Set Size to 4
steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Rhythm. Turn E3 once left so Size reads 4 and press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the eight-step loop is now cut into two four-step fragments, one for steps 1 to 4 and one for steps 5 to 8. On the grid only step 3 is bright: with the starting seed the first fragment comes from pattern 2 (a note on step 3 only) and the second from pattern 1, which has no notes in steps 5 to 8.

steps.title: Seed 0 picks the sparse draw
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays one C (MIDI 60) at velocity 100, a single note in the strip below. Seed 0 gives steps 1 to 4 to pattern 2 and steps 5 to 8 to pattern 1, which has no trigs there, and pattern 1's own E on step 3 is not mixed in.

steps.title: Pick seed 1
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Seed and turn E3 once right so it reads 1. The grid still shows the result of seed 0 until you apply the change.

steps.title: Apply seed 1
steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the grid now lights steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6. Seed 1 gives steps 1 to 4 to pattern 1 and steps 5 to 8 to pattern 2. Try other seeds, 2, 3 and so on, and listen for how each draw reshuffles the fragments.

steps.title: Each fragment keeps its source
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays pattern 1's C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and then pattern 2's C on step 6 at velocity 100. Each fragment keeps the notes and velocities of the pattern it came from.

scenes.title: Leave room around a leader’s anchors

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Two 8-step channels play at 90 BPM through the test device. Channel 1 (MIDI channel 1) has pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and pattern 2 (steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has pattern 3, a single trig on step 5, as its Foundation anchor. Channel 1 has no Interlock leader yet. The norns shows channel 1's Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

steps.title: Open Interlock
steps.caption: Select Interlock with E2 and press K3 to open the Interlock page for channel 1. This keeps channel 1's additions out of the way of another channel's anchors.

steps.title: Choose the leader
steps.caption: Select Leader and turn E3 once right to CH02. Channel 2 would lead channel 1; nothing changes until you apply.

steps.title: Apply: channel 2 leads
steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED, Window is 0 and Status reads ON. Step 5 goes dark on the grid because channel 1's addition starts exactly on channel 2's anchor. Steps 1 to 4 and step 7 stay lit.

steps.title: Only the coincidence is removed
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and step 7, and channel 2 plays its anchor on step 5 on MIDI channel 2. Nothing from channel 1 sounds on step 5.

steps.title: Edge case: widen the window while playing
steps.caption: The lesson above is complete; the next four steps are edge cases. Tap Play. While it plays, select Window, turn E3 twice right to 2 and press K3. The footer reads NEXT CYCLE: playback is still running, so Window 2 is queued and starts at the next loop.

steps.title: Edge case: a later draft is discarded
steps.caption: Window 2 is still queued. Turn E3 back to 0 as a new draft and press K2: the draft is discarded and Rhythm returns. Press K3 to reopen Interlock: Window still reads 2, the accepted value, not the discarded 0.

steps.title: Edge case: the window takes over at the loop boundary
steps.caption: After a few loops press Stop. The strip shows every loop played whole: the first loops with step 7, then without it once Window 2 took effect. The grid now shows steps 1 to 4.

steps.title: Select channel 2
steps.caption: Select channel 2 (grid (2,1)). The screen shows channel 2's Merge Shape list, ready to set a leader for it.

steps.title: Open channel 2's Interlock
steps.caption: Open Rhythm and then Interlock for channel 2: turn E2 to the row and press K3 each time. The header reads INTERLOCK CH02.

steps.title: Make channel 1 its leader
steps.caption: Select Leader and turn E3 once right to CH01. Channel 2 already leads channel 1, so this would make a chain.

steps.title: Edge case: a leader chain is refused
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply. The footer reads INVALID CHANNEL IS A LEADER: channel 2 already leads channel 1, so it cannot follow channel 1, and nothing changes.

steps.title: The refusal changes nothing
steps.caption: Press K2 to discard the draft and select channel 1 (grid (1,1)); the screen shows its Merge Shape list. Play two loops: Window 2 still applies, so channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and channel 2 plays step 5.

scenes.title: Snap Foundation anchors to a chord

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on the test device, the four-note melody C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) on steps 1 to 4. The additions of the Foundation phrase on steps 5 and 7 do not exist yet; you add them in the next step. No Harmony Ensemble group exists and Structure markers are off, so every note plays as written. The norns shows the Device page and the grid lights steps 1 to 4.

steps.title: Add the additions, open Ensemble
steps.caption: Hold step 1 (1,4) and tap step 8 (8,4) to loop eight steps. Open the pattern page (5,8), choose pattern 2 (2,1), tap trigs on steps 5 and 7, return to Channel (3,8) and assign pattern 2 (2,2). Then open Channel tasks > Harmony and choose Ensemble. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH01.

steps.title: Make the chord three notes
steps.caption: On the Ensemble list choose Create group and press K3 to make group 1. Select Template count with E2 and turn E3 to 3: the group's chord has three tones.

steps.title: Set Tone 2
steps.caption: Select Tone 2 with E2 and turn E3 to 2, two scale degrees above the root, which is E in C major.

steps.title: Set Tone 3
steps.caption: Select Tone 3 with E2 and turn E3 to 4, four scale degrees above the root, which is G. The chord is now C, E and G.

steps.title: Apply the chord
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply: the footer reads APPLIED.

steps.title: Open Members
steps.caption: Press K2 to return to the Ensemble list, select Members and press K3. The header reads MEMBERS CH01: the list of channels that follow the group's chord.

steps.title: Switch the group on
steps.caption: Set Group enabled to On with E3 and press K3. Voice count reads 1: channel 1, the only member, carries the chord on its own. The footer reads APPLIED.

steps.title: Turn Foundation on
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Merge Shape, set Mode to Foundation and press K3 to apply. Open Merge modes: Strategy and Active read FOUNDATION, so the four anchors on steps 1 to 4 plus the additions on steps 5 and 7 now play.

steps.title: Open Structure
steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Pitch, then choose Structure. Structure snaps chosen moments of the Foundation line to a chord while the notes in between keep their own pitch.

steps.title: Markers on anchors
steps.caption: Turn E3 once to set Markers to ANCHORS: every anchor onset now counts as a marker.

steps.title: Chord group one appears
steps.caption: A Chord group row appears showing 1, the Ensemble group you made. Structure needs an enabled group before Apply will accept the markers.

steps.title: Anchors snap to the chord
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then tap Play. Each anchor note snaps to the nearest chord tone, and a note exactly between two chord tones snaps to the lower one. Step 1 stays at 60, step 2 moves from 62 to 60, step 3 stays at 64 and step 4 moves from 65 to 64: the loop plays MIDI 60, 60, 64, 64 in the strip below. The added notes on steps 5 and 7 keep their own pitch and accent. Tap Play to stop.

steps.title: Check who deletion affects
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony > Ensemble and choose Delete group for group 1. A confirmation opens before anything is deleted; its Affected row reads 1, naming channel 1 as the channel that uses the group.

steps.title: Deletion restores authored pitches
steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm. Deleting the group also sets Markers to OFF in the same change. Tap Play: the anchors return to their written pitches, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65, and the added notes on steps 5 and 7 are unchanged. Tap Play to stop.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1 to 4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through the test device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (rate /1). Each step is a single voice: no chord notes are set and Harmony is Off. Playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Add a second voice
steps.caption: Open Masks for channel 1 and turn E3 one detent on Chd1, the first chord note. Chd1 reads 2nd: each step now sounds a second voice one scale step above its note, so the pairs are C+D, D+E, E+F and F+G (60+62, 62+64, 64+65, 65+67).

steps.title: Open Harmony
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony; the header reads VOICE LEADING CH01.

steps.title: Revoice the pairs
steps.caption: Set Mode to REVOICE and press K3 (Preset SMOOTH). Tap Play for two loops. Revoice keeps each pair's two pitch classes but chooses their octaves for the smoothest movement: both notes drop an octave to 48+50, 50+52, 52+53 and 53+55, at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97 in the strip below. Tap Stop.

scenes.title: Share a voicing while keeping each channel’s rhythm

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Four channels play through the test device, each on its own MIDI channel (1 to 4) with its own sparse rhythm: channel 1 plays the four-step phrase, channel 2 steps 1 and 3, channel 3 steps 2 and 4 and channel 4 step 4. Scale slot 1 (C major) is applied, Harmony is Off on every channel and no scale or octave locks are set, so each channel plays its own written pitches. A Harmony Ensemble group lets several channels share one chord: each member gets a role (Bass, Inner or Top), keeps its own rhythm, and takes its pitch from the group's shared voicing. The norns shows the Device page of channel 4.

steps.title: Create group 1 and open Members
steps.caption: On channel 1 open Channel tasks > Harmony, go to Groups, create group 1 with the Four-part smooth preset and open Members. The header reads MEMBERS CH01: this is where you choose which channels belong to the group.

steps.title: Assign the members, join channel 1
steps.caption: Assign channels 1 to 4 as the members, in order, with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save: the group is complete but still off. Press E1 back to the Harmony list, set Mode to ENSEMBLE with E3, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 1. Then select channel 2 (2,1): its Voice leading page opens.

steps.title: Join channel 2
steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 2. Then select channel 3 (3,1): its Voice leading page opens.

steps.title: Join channel 3
steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 3. Then select channel 4 (4,1): its Voice leading page opens.

steps.title: Join channel 4 and open Ensemble
steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 4. Then turn E2 to Ensemble and press K3. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH04.

steps.title: Switch the group on
steps.caption: On channel 4's Ensemble page select Group enabled and turn E3 to ON. Until now the group existed but did nothing.

steps.title: Four roles, four rhythms, one chord
steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then tap Play. Channels 1 to 4 take the roles Bass, Inner, Inner and Top. Each channel keeps its own rhythm and velocities, but all four take their pitch from one shared chord voicing: listen for a single chord spread across the four channels, MIDI 48, 55, 64 and 67 in the strip below. Tap Play to stop.

steps.title: Lock channel 2 to E major
steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) and set scale slot 3 to root E. Return to Channel (3,8), select channel 2, hold step 1 (1,4) and press slot 3 at (3,3) to lock that channel to E major. Tap Play and Stop, then open Harmony > Result for channel 2. The header reads VOICE MOVEMENT CH02.

steps.title: A scale lock bypasses the group
steps.caption: A scale lock on a member conflicts with the shared voicing, so channel 2 steps out of the Ensemble and plays its ordinary pitches: all five of its notes play MIDI 64 instead of 55, and Result reads LOCAL SCALE BYPASS.

steps.title: Give channel 3 its own octave
steps.caption: Select channel 3 (3,1) and press octave +1 at (11,8), then tap Play and Stop. Open Harmony: the Voice leading header for channel 3 reads OCT+1.

steps.title: Open Result for channel 3
steps.caption: Select Result in Voice leading and press K3: the Voice movement page for CH03 OCT+1 opens.

steps.title: An octave override bypasses too
steps.caption: A channel octave also leaves the shared voicing, so all six of channel 3's notes play MIDI 72 in the strip. In Result select Step with E2 and turn E3 to step 2. Result reads LOCAL OCTAVE BYPASS.
